name: corporate
note: A common enterprise data-classification policy. Each handling tag cites the reason it exists; carrying a tag does not make a deployment compliant with anything. Many policies call the top level HIGHLY CONFIDENTIAL: rename it in a copy of this file (a different scheme).

levels.name: INTERNAL
levels.reason: for staff and contractors; low harm if disclosed

levels.name: CONFIDENTIAL
levels.reason: limited to those who need it; harm if disclosed

levels.name: RESTRICTED
levels.reason: the most sensitive data; serious harm if disclosed

tokens.reason: protected health information under the HIPAA Privacy and Security Rules (45 CFR Parts 160 and 164)
personal data under privacy laws such as the GDPR (Art. 4(1)) and the CCPA/CPRA
cardholder data under PCI DSS v4.0
material non-public information (insider trading rules) and SOX-sensitive financial reporting
attorney-client privileged communications and attorney work product
trade secret protection requires reasonable secrecy measures (Defend Trade Secrets Act, 18 U.S.C. 1836)
customer data held under contract (NDA, MSA); CUSTOMER-<ID> keeps one customer's data from another's
technology subject to the EAR (15 CFR Parts 730-774): who may see it matters, not only how secret it is
